## mcrl monitor create

Create a monitor from a JSON or YAML file.

```text
Usage:
  mcrl monitor create -f <file> [flags]

Aliases:
  create, new

Create a monitor from a JSON or YAML file in the API's format.
Start from "mcrl monitor template <type>".

API: POST /api/v0/monitors
API key permission: Read, Write

Examples:
  mcrl monitor template host > cpu.yaml && vi cpu.yaml && mcrl monitor create -f cpu.yaml
  mcrl monitor get 'cpu high' --jq 'del(.id) | .name = "cpu high (staging)"' | mcrl monitor create -f -

Flags:
  -f, --file string   JSON or YAML file ("-" for stdin) (required)
```

## mcrl monitor delete

Delete a monitor.

```text
Usage:
  mcrl monitor delete <monitor>

Aliases:
  delete, rm

Delete a monitor. The output is the monitor as it was before deletion.

API: DELETE /api/v0/monitors/<id>
API key permission: Read, Write

Examples:
  mcrl monitor delete 'cpu high'
  mcrl monitor delete 2cSZzK3XfmG --yes
```

## mcrl monitor edit

Edit a monitor in $EDITOR.

```text
Usage:
  mcrl monitor edit <monitor>

Open the current monitor as YAML in $VISUAL or $EDITOR (default vi), then
show the changes and send them after confirmation.

The whole object is sent back, including fields mcrl does not know about,
so nothing is lost. Read-only fields (id) are hidden. If the file does not
parse, the editor opens again with the error at the top. Saving an empty file
or leaving it unchanged cancels.

API: PUT /api/v0/monitors/<id>
API key permission: Read, Write

Examples:
  mcrl monitor edit 3Ja1bAxcdef
  EDITOR='code --wait' mcrl monitor edit 3Ja1bAxcdef
```

## mcrl monitor get

Show a monitor.

```text
Usage:
  mcrl monitor get <monitor>

Aliases:
  get, show

Show a monitor by ID or name.

A reference that looks like an ID (11 alphanumeric characters) is looked up
as an ID first. Prefix it with "id:" or "name:" to force either.

API: GET /api/v0/monitors/<id>, GET /api/v0/monitors
API key permission: Read

Examples:
  mcrl monitor get 'cpu high'
  mcrl monitor get 2cSZzK3XfmG --jq '{name, isMute}'
```

## mcrl monitor list

List monitors.

```text
Usage:
  mcrl monitor list [flags]

Aliases:
  list, ls

List monitors, ordered by type and name.

--type and --name filter on the client side. --name matches a substring,
case-insensitively.

API: GET /api/v0/monitors
API key permission: Read

Examples:
  mcrl monitor list
  mcrl monitor list --type host --type service
  mcrl monitor list --name cpu --jq '.[] | {id, name, isMute}'

Flags:
      --name string        only monitors whose name contains this text
      --type stringArray   only monitors of this type (repeatable): host, connectivity, service, external, expression, anomalyDetection, query
```

## mcrl monitor mute

Mute monitors.

```text
Usage:
  mcrl monitor mute <monitor>...

Mute monitors. Only isMute is changed; the rest of each monitor is sent back as is.
The output is an array of the updated monitors.

API: GET /api/v0/monitors/<id>, PUT /api/v0/monitors/<id>
API key permission: Read, Write

Examples:
  mcrl monitor mute 'cpu high'
  mcrl monitor list --type host --jq '.[].id' | mcrl monitor mute -
```

## mcrl monitor template

Print a commented YAML template of a monitor.

```text
Usage:
  mcrl monitor template <type>

Print a commented YAML template of a monitor for "mcrl monitor create -f".
Types: host, connectivity, service, external, expression, anomalyDetection, query.

This is the only command that prints YAML: it is input for you to edit, not
API output.

Examples:
  mcrl monitor template host > cpu.yaml
  mcrl monitor template external
```

## mcrl monitor unmute

Unmute monitors.

```text
Usage:
  mcrl monitor unmute <monitor>...

Unmute monitors. Only isMute is changed; the rest of each monitor is sent back as is.
The output is an array of the updated monitors.

API: GET /api/v0/monitors/<id>, PUT /api/v0/monitors/<id>
API key permission: Read, Write

Examples:
  mcrl monitor unmute 'cpu high'
  mcrl monitor list --type host --jq '.[].id' | mcrl monitor unmute -
```

## mcrl monitor update

Update a monitor from a JSON or YAML file.

```text
Usage:
  mcrl monitor update <monitor> -f <file> [flags]

Update a monitor.

The API replaces the whole monitor: omitted fields such as isMute, scopes and
excludeScopes are reset. To avoid that, the fields in the file are merged
into the current monitor before sending, so the file only needs the fields
to change. --replace sends the file as the complete monitor instead.

API: GET /api/v0/monitors/<id>, PUT /api/v0/monitors/<id>
API key permission: Read, Write

Examples:
  echo 'warning: 85' | mcrl monitor update 'cpu high' -f -
  mcrl monitor update 2cSZzK3XfmG -f monitor.yaml --replace

Flags:
  -f, --file string            JSON or YAML file ("-" for stdin) (required)
      --replace[=true|false]   send the file as the complete monitor without merging
```
